transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, student health actually sent me here. They told me they can't clear me for these youth workshops I'm supposed to do because they say my weight is too low. I guess the number has kept dropping, but... I don't know, to me it just feels like what naturally happens when I’m really focused and busy with my classes.
When you think about your current weight, do you feel afraid of gaining weight or see yourself as heavier than others might say you are?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, even just the idea of gaining a single pound makes me panic. Um, if I were to eat a normal dinner, or... or eat something with butter in it, I feel like everyone would immediately be able to see it on me. Like they would just look at me and know I've completely lost my discipline.
Have you ever had episodes of eating a large amount of food and then felt you needed to get rid of it—by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising intensely to compensate?

No, I don't really do that. I don't eat large amounts of food to begin with, so there's never anything I feel like I need to throw up or use laxatives for. I do exercise, but it's just my regular routine to keep my weight where it is, not because I binged on something.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, or your most recent BMI if you know it?

Um, I'm actually not sure what my exact BMI is. When I was at student health, they weighed me and measured my height, but... they just told me the number was too low to clear me. I didn't actually look at the exact numbers they wrote down on the chart.
Do you happen to know your approximate height and current weight, even if you don't know the exact BMI?

Um, well, I know I'm about average height. But as for my weight... I really don't know. Like I said, I didn't look at the scale at student health, and I don't keep one in my dorm room. I usually just go by how my clothes fit and how I look in the mirror to keep track of things. So I don't actually have a number to give you.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether?

Um, I'm actually not sure. I haven't really been paying attention to that, to be honest. I don't keep track of my periods, so I couldn't tell you if they've changed or stopped. It's just not something I've noticed.
Do you know roughly how much weight you think you've lost over the past few months, even without exact numbers?

Um, I really couldn't give you a number for that either. Like I said, I don't weigh myself, so I don't know where I started or where I am now. I just know that some of my clothes fit a bit looser, but I honestly have no idea how much weight that actually means I've lost.
How long have you been feeling this way about your weight and limiting your food intake—weeks, months, or longer?

Um, it's been a few months, I think. Probably since the beginning of the semester. It's just... I pretty much plan my whole day around not really eating now. Like, I'll have black coffee before I go to studio, and maybe I'll take a few bites of something from the café later, but usually only if people are watching me and I need to look like I'm having something. I completely avoid bread or anything oily. It just feels like if I eat that stuff, it would undo all the control I've worked for.
Would you be willing to have your height and weight measured here today so we can calculate your current BMI together?

Um, no, I really don't want to do that. I've been avoiding the scale on purpose, so... stepping on one right now and figuring out my BMI would just really mess with my head. I'd really rather not know the exact numbers, to be honest.
Have you noticed things like feeling unusually cold all the time, dizziness, fainting, or your hair thinning or falling out more than usual?

Um, I haven't really noticed any of that, honestly. I don't feel dizzy or anything, and my hair seems totally normal. I mean, maybe I get a little cold sometimes, but it's winter, so I think that's pretty standard for anyone right now. But no, no fainting or anything serious like that.
Have friends, family, or professors made comments about you looking very thin or underweight recently?

Well, yeah, student health actually sent me here because they say my weight is too low. I guess the number has kept dropping, and they won't clear me to help with the youth workshops until I get checked out. But honestly, to me, it just feels like what happens when I'm focused and busy with my classes. I don't really see what they're seeing.
Would you be willing to be weighed and measured today if the results are not shared with you, so I can just note the numbers for your chart?

I don't know... I really don't think I can do that. Just the act of stepping on the scale is... it's just too much right now. 

Even if you don't tell me the number, I'll know you're taking it, and I'll just be sitting here trying to guess what it is and worrying about what you think of it. So... no, I'd really rather not do that today.
Do you think your current weight and eating habits are a problem for your health, or do you feel this is just how you need to be right now?

I know people keep saying it’s dangerous, but honestly, it feels really exaggerated to me. I don't think it's a health problem. It just feels like... like everyone is making my body the problem, when all I'm really doing is trying to stay sharp for school and my work. So yeah, I guess I do feel like this is just how I need to be right now.
